title: FedQueue: Queue-Aware Federated Learning for Cross-Facility HPC Training

split.decision: Official MNIST training data: fixed stratified 20% holdout via train_test_split(random_state=20261030): train 48000 / val 12000; ids original zero-based row indices sorted. Apply unchanged APPFL two-Dirichlet partition alpha1=8 alpha2=0.1, K=4 with BENCH_SEED to remaining train; select earliest best of 50 checkpoints on val. Official evaluation rows unchanged and held by judge.

baseline.paper_ref: Appendix E.4 Table 12, alpha_dir=0.1, published 88.7%; reproduced Max-A 88.96000000000001%. Benchmark selects on validation.

allowed_changes: Local optimizer, learning rates, aggregation, admission, scheduling and implementation for this fixed objective within those controls.
fixed_contract: Improve validation-selected MNIST accuracy by optimizing the fixed CNN/cross-entropy federated workload under the same queue, communication-round and local-work controls.
Table-9 SimpleCNN architecture, cross-entropy objective, pixels/255 and minibatch-64 work-counting convention.
Four clients, fixed two-Dirichlet partition, exogenous lognormal queue and genuine compute-time feedback.
50 target rounds; all returned scheduler Ek work <=1.2 times the frozen baseline mean; original selection/accuracy rules.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Queue delays stay unknown until a client reports them: budgeting and admission may use only delays already observed, not the queue RNG, its seed, or a delay sampled for the current round.
Replacing CNN/objective, changing batch granularity to obtain more work, centralizing client data or changing client/queue processes.
Exceeding the algorithmic local-work budget or selecting checkpoints using hidden labels.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
Copies of this data from an installed package count as external data (patch audit).
